relations.subject: Taixu
relations.evidence: one of the modern Buddhist academies (Minnan Buddhist Institute 閩南佛學院) set up by Master Taixu (1890–1947)

relations.subject: Yinshun
relations.evidence: He was ordained in October and subsequently enrolled at one of the modern Buddhist academies (Minnan Buddhist Institute 閩南佛學院)

relations.subject: Yinshun
relations.evidence: After he recovered from sickness, he went back to the Minnan Buddhist Institute but was invited to teach his classmates.

relations.subject: Yinshun
relations.evidence: In between, he went to Wuchang Buddhist Institute 武昌佛學院 where he studied exegeses of the three-treatise or Sanlun lineage 三論宗

relations.subject: Yinshun
relations.evidence: Master Taixu asked him to go to Wuchang Buddhist Institute to lead a few students to study the three treatises. Although he was reluctant to go, he still went to Wuchang in 1937.

relations.subject: Yinshun
relations.evidence: Fazun's views on Tibetan Buddhism deeply influenced Master Yinshun who would incorporate them into his understanding of the Dharma.

relations.subject: Yinshun
relations.evidence: Besides the influence of Master Taixu's writing, Master Yinshun considered Venerable Fazun to be a truly special causal condition in his learning of the Dharma.

relations.subject: Yinshun
relations.evidence: he was chosen to be the president of the Hong Kong Buddhist Association (Xianggang fojiao lianhehui 香港佛教聯合會).

relations.subject: Yinshun
relations.evidence: he went to Taiwan in 1952, where he was invited to be one of the mentor-teachers 導師 at Shandao Monastery 善導寺.
